prompts.text: What can a team's reaction to an error tell you about its working culture?
Describe a mistake at work that led to a genuinely useful process change.
Investigate why a problem happened or focus first on preventing it from happening again?
A colleague discovers a reporting error just before a presentation. How should the team handle the correction?
People are more likely to raise concerns early when mistakes aren't treated as personal failures.
A useful post-project review should identify the system conditions, not just the person who noticed the problem last.
What makes it easier for you to admit that an approach isn't working?
Recall someone acknowledging an oversight in a way that increased your trust.
A new teammate follows an outdated instruction and causes confusion. What should the team examine?
Run a short review immediately after a project or collect lessons for a scheduled meeting?
Which part of a workplace would you redesign to make everyday tasks easier?
Tell me about entering a workspace that seemed unusually well thought out.
Improve the lighting and acoustics or simplify the tools everyone has to use?
A team has limited funds to improve its office. What information should it gather from employees?
Small environmental details can affect how easily people concentrate and collaborate.
A beautiful office isn't automatically a productive or accessible workplace.
Which physical workplace feature would make the biggest difference to your daily comfort?
Recall adapting to an unfamiliar work environment and discovering what you missed.
Several employees require different kinds of workspaces. How might a team make the layout flexible?
Quiet individual work areas or open collaboration spaces with reservable rooms?
What do you find most interesting about how different organisations make decisions?
Describe watching a leader explain a difficult choice to a team.
Learn how decisions are approved or how managers measure their long-term results?
A new policy affects several departments differently. What questions should leaders ask before announcing it?
An organisation's values become clearer when its choices involve trade-offs.
Explaining why a decision was made can matter as much as announcing what happens next.
Which decision do you think frontline employees should be consulted on more often?
Recall a small suggestion from staff changing the direction of a project.
Two departments disagree about priorities and both have reasonable concerns. Who should be heard first?
A transparent decision record or regular open forums where employees can raise questions?
How do you distinguish a useful performance measure from one that encourages shortcuts?
Tell me about working towards a target that turned out to be less meaningful than expected.
Measure how quickly tasks are completed or how well the results serve their purpose?
A customer support team handles calls faster but customer issues remain unresolved. What would you investigate?
A metric can become misleading when people forget the question it was meant to answer.
Teams should be able to explain the limitations of their own success measures.
Which aspect of good work is hardest to turn into a simple number?
Recall somebody drawing attention to a hidden improvement that wasn't reflected in a dashboard.
Your team can measure only three things about a new service. How would you choose them?
Review a broad set of performance signals or track a few measures with clear explanations?
What helps you understand the needs of people who use a product or service?
Describe observing a customer struggle with something the designers believed was simple.
Watch people use a prototype or interview them about their current difficulties?
A business receives repeated complaints that a form is confusing. What would you ask users to demonstrate?
People often adapt to bad systems so thoroughly that they stop describing them as problems.
A customer's workaround can reveal more than a polished description of a feature.
Which service do you think would improve if its designers watched people use it in everyday conditions?
Recall an interaction with a helpful employee that changed your opinion of a business.
Two user groups want opposing changes to the same product. What further research would help?
Improve one frustrating step in a service or add a frequently requested new capability?
Which ethical dilemma in ordinary work deserves more open discussion?
Tell me about a time somebody protected another person's privacy during a routine task.
Discuss how to report a concern safely or how teams should handle confidential information?
A coworker casually shares customer details in a group chat. What's a proportionate way to address it?
A workplace's approach to ethics often becomes visible through routine decisions, not dramatic cases.
Doing what's convenient isn't a sufficient reason to ignore somebody's privacy.
Which professional responsibility should every new employee understand from the beginning?
Recall a situation where asking for permission was important even though the task seemed harmless.
You're asked to use an automated tool on sensitive records. What questions would you ask about safeguards?
Learn more about conflicts of interest or the practical handling of personal data?
What makes an interview question help you understand an employer rather than simply impress it?
Describe discovering something important about a job only after talking with its current employees.
Ask a hiring manager why people stay on their team or what challenges a new employee should expect?
An offer sounds appealing but its day-to-day responsibilities are vague. How might you clarify them?
The interview process can reveal how an organisation communicates under pressure.
Candidates should be able to ask serious questions without being treated as disloyal.
Which part of a job description would you ask an employer to explain in concrete examples?
Recall being surprised by a thoughtful question during a professional interview.
Two positions offer similar pay but very different schedules. What information would make comparison easier?
Choose a role after speaking to future teammates or after reviewing a realistic sample assignment?
What has observing a good manager taught you about helping other people perform well?
Tell me about somebody who delegated a responsibility and trusted you to find a solution.
Receive clear expectations with freedom to choose methods or close guidance while learning?
A team leader notices one person doing most of the difficult tasks. How should they assess the workload?
Good management often involves removing obstacles that individual employees can't control.
A leader's willingness to ask for feedback is more important than appearing to know every answer.
What is a sign a manager has understood the strengths of different team members?
Recall an occasion when a leader gave credit to the person whose work was least visible.
A new supervisor inherits a team with a strained relationship. What should they learn before making changes?
Have regular one-to-one conversations or hold open team discussions about recurring challenges?
What makes a professional community worth participating in over several years?
Describe an event where you learnt something valuable from a person in an unrelated field.
Attend a small skills-sharing group or join a larger professional conference?
You're organising a community for people at different career stages. How would you make discussions useful to beginners?
Professional communities can become more valuable when people share what hasn't worked.
The quality of a network depends more on reciprocity than the number of contacts.
Which topic would make you attend a professional meetup even after a tiring workday?
Recall someone recommending a resource that helped you solve a problem months later.
An online community becomes dominated by a handful of experts. How could organisers invite newer voices?
Share an unfinished project for feedback or discuss useful lessons from a completed one?
How has the meaning of career success changed for people around you?
Tell me about somebody finding satisfaction in a role others considered unremarkable.
Explore how different workers define stability or what gives them a sense of achievement?
A friend wants a less demanding job even though it pays less. What might matter in their decision?
People's career priorities often shift alongside their responsibilities outside work.
A fulfilling career is not always the one with the fastest promotion path.
What do you hope your working life makes possible beyond your job title?
Recall meeting someone who had designed an unusual balance between work and other commitments.
You're asked to describe your ideal career without mentioning salary or prestige. What would you include?
Choose greater flexibility in familiar work or a more challenging role with a predictable schedule?
